newsitem.title: UK: Japan venture, new sales boost Amersham half-year.
newsitem.headline: Japan venture, new sales boost Amersham half-year.

text.p: British radioactive healthcare and science services company Amersham International said on Tuesday that profitability gains and fast-selling new technology lifted first-half earnings and should underpin future growth.
Amersham's pretax profits rose by 43 percent to 28.4 million pounds ($47 million) in the six months to September 30 and it raised the interim dividend 22 percent to 6.0 pence per share.
Chief executive Bill Castell welcomed a big jump in heathcare profitability and said there should be more to come.
He also said the life sciences business, which sells specialist support systems to pharmaceutical researchers, had passed an important milestone in its sales to the drug industry.
Investors were heartened by Amersham's broad-based progress, as well as the generous payout, and its stock price strengthened after the figures and share analysts' positive comments.
By 1300 GMT the shares were up 22.5 pence at 1025 pence, for a net rise of 2.2 percent, in firm turnover.
Castell told Reuters that Amersham was now benefiting from full distribution capacity for each of its core businesses in all major markets -- namely the United States, Japan and Europe.
For healthcare, he said its enlarged interest in Japanese venture NMP and new U.S. distributors had brought "a step change in profitability and a step change in distribution capability".

A surge in U.S. turnover, up 27 percent in the half, was heralded by the approval by the FDA of Amersham's key Myoview radioactive heart-imaging agent during the spring and should go on, Castell predicted.
"In the near-term, I expect us to continue with good growth because we're taking out more innovative products," he said.
The Nihon Medi-Physics (NMP) joint venture, co-owned with Sumitomo Chemical, became healthcare's star profit performer.
Amersham's interest contributed 4.3 million pounds to the division's profit before interest and tax of 14.1 million pounds and Castell described this result as ahead of expectations.
He said life science services was also shifting towards higher growth segments, especially in genome-based work.

An indicator of this was its fast growing client list among pharmaceutical companies, where he saw great potential. During the half such industrial sales passed 50 percent of the total for the first time, reaching 53 percent, he said.

Castell said he believed the genome-based market was set to become "the major growth market" for the future and the company was well placed to support the drug industry's progress in that direction when its work becomes increasingly based on genetic understanding rather than on cellular understanding.
As a whole, the life science division produced an 11 percent increase in profits before interest and tax of 17.3 million pounds -- a level of growth achieved without raising costs.
Share analysts said that the solid performance from this division combined with a powerful result from healthcare.

"The two important divisions... were usefully better, aided a bit by favourable currency movements. The big change is the way the Japanese joint venture is treated and that's helped results quite a lot," said SocGen analyst Paul Diggle, who added the more generous dividend rise than before would be welcomed. ($1=.6050 Pound)
